dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real-valued function e on Fin n, this is its norm under the standard finite function-space normed-ring structure, namely the maximum of |e(i)| over i in Fin n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the left-hand side of the asserted inequality, the maximum absolute coordinate of e.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For e on Fin n, this is LocalDef003(e) divided by the real square root of the real cast of n, hence sqrt(sum_i e(i)^2) / sqrt(n).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the normalized Euclidean magnitude multiplied by sqrt(n) on the right-hand side.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: For e on Fin n, this is the real square root of LocalDef004(e), namely sqrt(sum_i e(i)^2).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the numerator in LocalDef002 and represents the Euclidean norm of e.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: For e on Fin n, this is the finite sum over all i in Fin n of e(i) raised to the second power.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the sum of coordinate squares beneath the square root in the right-hand side.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin n is the finite type of natural-number indices i satisfying i < n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes e an n-coordinate real vector and determines the index set of the finite sum and maximum.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This selects heterogeneous multiplication from an HMul instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the supplied real instance, it makes the right-hand side the ordinary real product sqrt(n) times LocalDef002(e).

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: This selects the less-than-or-equal relation from an LE instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the real-order instance, it expresses the asserted ordinary real inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.meaning: This selects the strict less-than relation from an LT instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the natural-number instance, it expresses the hypothesis 0 < n.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the type of natural numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It restricts the dimension n to a natural number.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat.cast

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat

dependency_coverage.name: Real

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE

binders: n is an implicitly quantified natural number.
e is an arbitrary function Fin n → Real, equivalently an n-coordinate real vector.
conclusions: The maximum absolute coordinate of e satisfies max_{i in Fin n} |e(i)| ≤ sqrt(n) · (sqrt(sum_{i in Fin n} e(i)^2) / sqrt(n)). Since n > 0, this is equivalently max_{i in Fin n} |e(i)| ≤ sqrt(sum_{i in Fin n} e(i)^2).
mathematical_definitions: I_n = Fin n = {i in Nat : i < n}.
L(e) = sqrt(S(e)), the Euclidean norm of e.
R(e) = L(e) / sqrt(n), the root-mean-square magnitude of the coordinates.
N(e) = max_{i in I_n} |e(i)|, the finite supremum norm.
The asserted inequality is N(e) ≤ sqrt(n) · R(e).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every positive natural-number dimension n and every real vector e with n coordinates, the largest absolute coordinate of e is at most the square root of n times the root-mean-square magnitude of its coordinates. Equivalently, the maximum absolute coordinate is at most the Euclidean norm.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimension is restricted to natural numbers and the substantive assertion assumes n > 0.
For n = 0, the outer implication has a false antecedent, so that branch of the universally quantified proposition is vacuous.
Positivity of n ensures that sqrt(n) is nonzero, so the division in LocalDef002 is mathematically well-defined without division by zero.
Lean's real division is total even at zero, but that convention does not affect the positive-dimensional case.
No restrictions are imposed on the real coordinates of e.
The proposition states only the upper bound; it does not state equality conditions, strictness, optimality, or any converse or lower bound.
